candidates.title: Sampling Where It Matters: Predicting LLM Serving Performance
candidates.abstract: Characterizing Large Language Model (LLM) serving performance is a combinatorial problem where a suboptimal choice wastes profiling budget: every change in model, hardware, or software version requires fresh profiling, yet exhaustive benchmarking is infeasible. Existing approaches - simulators and static performance estimators - lose fidelity on novel architectures or target only optima. We introduce Predictive Kernel Herding (PKH), a sampler which reformulates Random Forest leaf co-occurrence as linear-time histogram matching, replacing O(N2) kernel comparisons. On four real-world LLM serving traces spanning 3,000+ configurations, PKH is the only sampler that delivers top-ranked accuracy on both throughput and latency predictions, dominating the cost-accuracy Pareto frontier. PKH predicts output throughput within 10% MAPE and mean Time to First Token (TTFT) within 20% MAPE, reaching practically useful accuracy with up to 1.6× lower profiling time than the next-best method at equivalent error.
candidates.reason: 著者所属IBM Researchの一次公開要旨。Predictive Kernel Herdingにより3,000超のLLMサービング構成の性能測定点を選択し、4実トレースで出力throughputを10%以内のMAPE、平均TTFTを20%以内のMAPEで予測。比較法と同等誤差に達するプロファイル時間を最大1.6倍削減。実際のLLMサービング性能推定・プロファイリング予算最適化を直接扱う。
